page.overview:
Who is Ondoher?

Ondoher was the thirty-first King of Gondor.

Ondoher succeeded his father Calimehtar in TA 1936. During his time the rulers of Gondor and Arthedain became aware that a power was coordinating attacks on the Exiles of Númenor, leading to the two kingdoms to renew contact and form an alliance. Ondoher's daughter Fíriel married Prince Arvedui of Arthedain. In TA 1944, the Wainriders invaded Gondor from the east while their allies, the Haradrim, invaded Gondor from the south. Ondoher and his eldest son and heir, Artamir, led the main army close to the Black Gate, where they clashed with the Wainriders. The left wing of Ondoher's army was commanded by Adrahil, the Prince of Dol Amroth. The right wing was commanded by Minohtar, the captain of Gondor's armies. The center was commanded by Ondoher himself.

In the ensuing battle Ondoher was slain together with Artamir, and Gondor was defeated. The rearguard of the army defended Ithilien while Adrahil joined up with General Eärnil, who had defeated the Haradrim.

Although Eärnil finally defeated the Wainriders, it was learned that Ondoher's second son Faramir (not to be confused with Faramir, brother of Boromir) was slain with his father, despite a law requiring that at least one heir should be left behind.
